_readme: Data only. Single source of crop values for the planner. Keys are the registry crop ids. Adding a crop = adding an entry, not code. Every value has a 'source'. FAO-56 = Allen et al. 1998; facts checked in docs/research/fao56.md.

kc_ini.source: FAO-56 Table 12, Solanaceae group row, footnote 1 (the 'Kc ini' header is an image, identified by position)

kc_mid.source: FAO-56 Table 12, tomato, footnote 2 (staked tomato would be 1.20, not used)

kc_end.source: FAO-56 Table 12 gives the range 0.70-0.90 and no rule inside it. 0.80 = middle of the range, owner decision (judgment log)

height_m.source: FAO-56 Table 12, tomato, max crop height h

stage_rows.source: FAO-56 Table 11, tomato. Default: Mediterranean row (closest to the Negev plots)

kc_ini.source: FAO-56 Table 12, Solanaceae group row, footnote 1 (the 'Kc ini' header is an image, identified by position)

kc_mid.source: FAO-56 Table 12, sweet peppers (bell), footnote 2 (staked pepper would be 1.15, not used)

height_m.source: FAO-56 Table 12, sweet peppers (bell), max crop height h

stage_rows.source: FAO-56 Table 11, sweet peppers (bell). Table prints init as '25/30'; 30 chosen because 30+35+40+20 = 125 (inference, not stated by FAO). Default: Mediterranean row
